blurb: Japan's oldest and largest museum, in Ueno Park.

facts.t: It began with an exhibition at the Yushima Seidō in 1872, just after the Meiji Restoration, when Japan was opening to the world. It holds about 120,000 objects, including 89 National Treasures.
Hasegawa Tōhaku's Pine Trees screens, painted in ink around 1595, show trees vanishing into fog. They are a National Treasure and come out only for a few weeks each New Year.
